newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Appeal of Hungarian shares to shrink - Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Appeal of Hungarian shares to shrink - Nomura.

text.p: Hungary will remain a core market for foreign share investors in eastern Europe, but the percentage of invested assets allocated to the country is likely to drop, London-based Nomura Research said on Wednesday.
"Investors put new money into larger, cheaper markets," Nomura analyst Frances Cloud told an international conference on Hungarian capital markets.
The BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) more than doubled this year, but Cloud said there were factors limiting further rises.
Many Hungarian shares already had high valuation and the relatively low capitalisation of the market was not likely to increase substantially in the near future, she said.
Cloud said the capitalisation of the BSE totalled only $4.6 billion, and possible privatisation issues in the next two years could only add $3 billion at the most.
"Even after these issues, the market will remain small," Nomura said in a statement released at the conference.

Cloud added that private company listings in Hungary were not likely to boost the BSE's capitalisation as private firms' need for equity financing was declining and they were reluctant to publish more information about themselves.
She said foreign investors would continue to dominate the market in the next two or three years.
Most of the trading in Hungarian shares goes through London's SEAQ rather than the BSE and Cloud said the role of London was likely to strengthen as more U.S. investors entered the market.
"Currently about half of the money coming to the BSE is from the U.S., and that's much more than earlier," she said. "Some 30 percent of the free float is in U.S. hands."
U.S. investors required good liquidity and the best execution from the market they traded on, Nomura said.

The role of domestic investors was not likely to increase in Hungary in the short-term as it did not plan mass privatisation, bank accounts offered relatively high returns and Hungarians have not discovered the attractions of capital investments, Cloud said.
However, she added that the planned reform of the social security system, which was likely to help the spread of private pension funds, may increase domestic demand for Hungarian shares.

Cloud said the Hungarian capital market was likely to remain important as the country's economy showed signs of improvement, bourse companies were of high quality and accounting standards remained the best in the region.
